claims.sentence: On 8 July 2026 the WHO published its Global status report on cancer 2026, projecting that new cancer cases will nearly double by 2050 without urgent action.
claims.evidence: WHO news item 08-07-2026 'projected to nearly double by 2050'; report 'Global status report on cancer 2026'.

claims.sentence: The WHO released its Global status report on cancer 2026 on 8 July 2026.
The WHO says annual new cancer cases could rise to nearly 35 million by 2050 without urgent action.
claims.evidence: 'annual cancer cases are projected to rise to nearly 35 million by 2050'.

claims.sentence: It estimates about 20.6 million new cases and close to 10 million deaths each year at present.
claims.evidence: 'estimated 20.6 million new cases and close to 10 million deaths annually'.

claims.sentence: The report makes seven recommendations across three shifts: better capabilities, better protections and better value.
claims.evidence: Seven recommendations grouped under three strategic shifts: better capabilities, better protections, better value.

claims.sentence: On 8 July 2026 the World Health Organization (WHO) published its Global status report on cancer 2026 and called for urgent action.
claims.evidence: News item dated 8 July 2026 calling for urgent action.

claims.sentence: The WHO says cancer now causes an estimated 20.6 million new cases and close to 10 million deaths a year, making it the second leading cause of death worldwide after cardiovascular disease.
claims.evidence: 'second leading cause of death globally, after cardiovascular disease'.

claims.sentence: Without urgent action, it projects annual new cases rising to nearly 35 million by 2050.
claims.evidence: Nearly 35 million by 2050 without urgent action.

claims.sentence: The WHO says nearly four in ten cancer cases are linked to preventable risk factors.
claims.evidence: Summary of July report: nearly four in ten cases linked to preventable risk factors (separate Feb 2026 WHO/IARC study gives 37%).

claims.sentence: The report sets out seven recommendations grouped under three shifts: better capabilities, better protections and better value.
It points to underinvestment in prevention, unequal access to diagnosis and treatment, and insufficient social protection.
claims.evidence: Report highlights underinvestment in prevention, unequal access to diagnostics and treatment, insufficient social protections.

claims.sentence: The WHO's first global survey of people affected by cancer, with more than 4,000 respondents in 116 countries, found widespread psychological distress among patients and caregivers.
claims.evidence: Survey of more than 4000 people affected by cancer across 116 countries; widespread psychological distress among patients and caregivers.

notes: Date 8 July 2026 consistent across WHO and IARC (pr383). 'Nearly double' is WHO's headline; 35 million vs 20.6 million is about 70% rise, so keep WHO's wording attributed. IARC GLOBOCAN 2024 gives 34.4 million by 2050 (different source, not conflicting). c09 four in ten partly relies on a blended summary; Feb 2026 study says 37% for 2022.
